title: Admin password card: three things decided in chat

steps.headline: The first version handles your computer's admin password only; keys and other logins come later as their own projects.
steps.changed: Replaces your 'any password' pick. You chose this order in chat: admin password first, then API keys and .env values, then GitHub/SSH logins. Both are filed on the roadmap.
steps.notice: A command asking for a website, SSH or database password still fails from chat, as it does today, until those projects ship.

steps.path: A phone or browser paired to your computer
steps.headline: Typing your admin password from your paired phone or browser is allowed; the leftover risks are acceptable.
steps.changed: The risk you asked me to evaluate: only your Tailscale devices can reach the app, the link is encrypted, and your remote password guards it. What's left: someone holding your unlocked, signed-in phone (they'd still need your admin password), a phone browser that ignores 'don't save this', or a taken-over Tailscale account.
steps.notice: Admin commands can be unblocked away from your desk.

steps.path: When a command asks for admin
steps.headline: When 'sudo' is written in the command, the password is asked right after you approve, before anything runs; hidden admin steps ask midway.
steps.changed: Your note asked for up front where possible. It is possible whenever the command visibly uses sudo. A script that hides its admin step can't be known in advance, so that case asks partway through.
steps.notice: Most admin commands ask for everything before they start.
